hi there -

your partial code is missing several dependencies that I'm unfamiliar with, utc_time(), UTCDateTime, nor does it illustrate what usage of the custom constuct is failing.   The [MCVE](http://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve) below runs without failure on 1.3 so please provide complete information, thanks!

```python
import datetime

import pytz

from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy import Date
from sqlalchemy import DateTime
from sqlalchemy import Integer
from sqlalchemy import Time
from sqlalchemy.ext.compiler import compiles
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.ext.hybrid import hybrid_property
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from sqlalchemy.sql import expression

Base = declarative_base()


class SplittedCreateTimeMixin:
    """Mixin for a splitted create time"""

    _create_date = Column(
        "create_date",
        Date,
        nullable=False,
        # server_default=utc_date()  # don't have this
    )
    _create_time = Column(
        "create_time",
        Time,
        nullable=False,
        # server_default=utc_time()  # don't have this
    )

    @hybrid_property
    def create_time(self):
        """create time property"""
        return datetime.combine(
            self._create_date, self._create_time, tzinfo=pytz.UTC
        )

    @create_time.setter
    def create_time(self, value):
        """create time setter"""
        self._create_date = value.date()
        self._create_time = value.time()

    @create_time.expression
    def create_time(self):
        """create time expression"""
        # use a label to allow the usage in sub-selects
        return combine_date_time(self._create_date, self._create_time).label(
            "create_timestamp"
        )


class A(SplittedCreateTimeMixin, Base):
    __tablename__ = "a"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


class combine_date_time(expression.FunctionElement):
    """Concat of date and time."""

    name = "datetime"
    type = DateTime()  # don't have UTCDateTime


@compiles(combine_date_time, "sqlite")
def sqlite_combine_date_time(element, compiler, **kw):
    """sqlite compile of combine_date_time"""

    return "datetime(%s)" % compiler.process(element.clauses, **kw)


e = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(e)
s = Session(e)

s.query(A.create_time).all()

```

Hello all,

I was now finally able to extract all code which is needed and to simply it in less than 100 lines :-). I updates my initial comment with the new example and error stack.

Best regards, Kai

Hi,
thanks for the explanation. 
When we started with our application. we didn't specify by purpose a default clause but always related to a dialect. We support two databases and there is just no default. So in reality, combine_date_time has two implementations: one for sqlite and one for SAP HANA. As you can see, I can't choose a default. 
In addition, while creating this example, I played with the code, as far as I can remember removing e.g. the top clause also prevents the error.

Therefore it would be good to know if this is intended or not and if yes, when you support multiple dialects which one should be the default.

Thanks a lot, Kai

this is the current test case

```python
from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import DateTime
from sqlalchemy import Integer
from sqlalchemy import MetaData
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy import Table
from sqlalchemy.ext.compiler import compiles
from sqlalchemy.sql import expression


class combine_date_time(expression.FunctionElement):
    name = "datetime"
    type = DateTime()


# @compiles(combine_date_time)
# def combine_date_time(element, compiler, **kw):
#    return "DEFINITELY NOT USED"


@compiles(combine_date_time, "sqlite")
def sqlite_combine_date_time(element, compiler, **kw):
    return "datetime(%s)" % compiler.process(element.clauses, **kw)


t1 = Table("t1", MetaData(), Column("q", Integer))

a1 = t1.alias()

stmt = select([combine_date_time(t1.c.q)])
stmt = select([stmt.alias()])

cols = stmt.c


```

So there's a few angles to this at the same time:

1. the bug itself is that we should be catching compilation exception when we call str().  it is currently catching UnsupportedCompilation so I think the compiles extension simply needs to raise the right exception subclas.

2. the fact that we call str() at all is a little bit frivolous but this is not worth changing in 1.3.   in 1.4 it might be, this is how it's used:

```python
from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import DateTime
from sqlalchemy import Integer
from sqlalchemy import MetaData
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy import Table
from sqlalchemy.ext.compiler import compiles
from sqlalchemy.sql import expression
from sqlalchemy.dialects import sqlite
from sqlalchemy import __version__


class combine_date_time(expression.FunctionElement):
    name = "datetime"
    type = DateTime()


@compiles(combine_date_time)
def _combine_date_time(element, compiler, **kw):
    return "DEFINITELY_NOT_USED"


@compiles(combine_date_time, "sqlite")
def sqlite_combine_date_time(element, compiler, **kw):
    return "datetime(%s)" % compiler.process(element.clauses, **kw)


t1 = Table("t1", MetaData(), Column("q", Integer))

stmt = select([combine_date_time(t1.c.q)])

if "1.4" in __version__:
    stmt = stmt.alias()

# if we don't use the stringify, then this label isn't here
print(
    select([stmt.c["DEFINITELY_NOT_USED"]]).compile(dialect=sqlite.dialect())
)

```

but for here we will just address the exception being thrown.
